in_text_mentions: The planned surgery was a thoracoscopic-assisted subtotal esophagectomy with laparoscopic-assisted gastric resection and gastric tube reconstruction. A combined approach with general anesthesia and epidural anesthesia was planned. Due to the requirement for one-lung ventilation during the thoracoscopic procedure, double-lumen tube (DLT) intubation was initially planned. Preoperative chest X-rays revealed a slight narrowing of the tracheal diameter (Figure 2), but a diagnosis of CTS was not made at that time.

The second diagnostic trigger was the finding of tracheal stenosis on a preoperative chest X-ray (Figure 2). However, the degree of stenosis was not pronounced enough, and the attending anesthesiologist did not pursue further investigation. As a result of this, three attempts of intubation were done. And the patient’s risk of complications was higher than usual [26]. Upon reviewing the CT scan (Figure 3), it was clear that there are complete tracheal rings and tracheal stenosis, and the difficulty with DLT intubation could have been predicted preoperatively. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Panel A is a CT image showing circumferential tracheal narrowing associated with complete tracheal rings, which is the primary target disease. B: Panel B is a CT image showing circumferential tracheal narrowing consistent with complete tracheal rings. C: Panel C is a CT image showing circumferential tracheal narrowing consistent with complete tracheal rings. D: Panel D is a CT image showing circumferential tracheal narrowing consistent with complete tracheal rings. E: Panel E shows a 3D reconstruction revealing a pulmonary artery sling and unusual pulmonary artery origin, a finding associated with the patient's known CTS. F: Panel F is a 3D reconstruction showing a tracheal bronchus and precise measurement of tracheal narrowing (6 mm), findings related to the patient's CTS.

The left pulmonary artery originated from the right pulmonary artery and encircled the trachea (E). MPA, main pulmonary artery; RPA, right pulmonary artery; LPA, left pulmonary artery; T, trachea

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a bronchoscopy image showing the absence of the membranous trachea and presence of complete tracheal rings, directly corresponding to the primary diagnosis in the case report. B: Panel B is a bronchoscopy image showing membranous tissue at the bifurcation, a specific finding observed during the case study. C: Panel C is a bronchoscopy image showing petechiae of the mucosa, which is a clinical manifestation observed in this case report.
